items.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Ferrer directly addresses the central grounding burden by identifying an unchanging necessary consciousness as the proposed truth maker for moral facts independent of contingent human attitudes. Principal limitation: The presentation characterizes divine necessity as maximal grounding but supplies insufficient independent justification that this mind exists or that locating value within its attitudes avoids subjectivism rather than relocating it. Live burden: He must establish a principled connection between divine nature and normative authority while explaining why necessary consciousness generates obligations that impersonal facts or shared human interests cannot generate.

items.currentText: Showed how chosen goals can support publicly checkable consequence assessments.
items.lockedProposition: Even an initially chosen goal such as well-being permits assessment of actions by their consequences without requiring an intrinsic cosmic purpose.

items.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Dillahunty offers a concrete evaluative method in which consequences can be compared against wellbeing while candidly acknowledging that the concept remains incompletely defined and initially selected. Principal limitation: Objective measurement after choosing a goal does not itself establish that everyone morally ought to choose that goal leaving Ferrer's categorical challenge intact at the foundational level. Live burden: He must distinguish practical objectivity within a shared commitment from universal normative authority and explain why sufficiently informed agents should privilege wellbeing when interests conflict or sacrifice becomes personally costly.
